content.title: DU defeats Wisconsin to claim Frozen Four championship
content.text: Booth began his high school career at Cheery Creek and now is back in the Centennial State for college hoops FORT COLLINS, Colo. — After three years away, Carey Booth finally came home. "It's pretty much like everybody that leaves Colorado," Colorado State head coach Ali Farokhmanesh said. "You always wanna make your way back at some point." Booth, the Rams starting center, started his high school career at Cherry Creek before transferring to powerhouse prep school Brewster Academy in New Hampshire. "It was kind of hard, obviously," Booth, a junior, said about leaving home for his final year of high school. "For me, I just thought of it as going to college a year early, and I think it was a beneficial decision for me." He signed with Notre Dame out of high school, making 19 starts as a true freshman before he transferred to Illinois. While with the Illini for his sophomore season, his playing time and numbers shrank, leading him to enter the transfer portal for a second time. "The biggest thing for me was the opportunity," Booth said. "I played at prestigious schools, obviously, but for me, experience is most important and being able to play and obviously having that opportunity here was a big factor." That's what brought him back to Colorado to sign with the Rams. "I'll be honest, the first two times were really hard recruiting him," Farokhmanesh said. "And then the third time ... I called him and then I was like, 'You wanna come?' He said yes, and that was it. So it was the easiest recruitment ever." It helped that Farokhmanesh has known Booth since his high school days. "I took an unofficial [visit] here as a sophomore in high school, so they've kind of always been like in the mix, obviously," Booth said. "I've had a relationship with Ali for a while. Ali was my lead recruiter. He was the assistant that would always call me or check in and contact me." Beyond having a relationship with Carey, Farokhmanesh also had one with his dad, Calvin, who was the Nuggets' general manager for five seasons, helping lead Denver to its lone championship in 2023. That pedigree, combined with Carey's skill, made him a highly sought-after recruit. "We want to get to the point where we're always getting the best kid in Colorado to stay home," Farokhmanesh said. "I think that's important not only for our fan base, but I think it means a little something different when you're playing for that Colorado State on your chest every night out." So far it's been a perfect pairing. Booth is averaging nearly 12 points a game and has a team-high seven assists, both of which are career highs. "I'm not really surprised," Booth said of his stats. "I kind of knew when I got the opportunity I wasn't gonna look back. This is I've known I could do, and I'm glad that I'm able to show it. "Being in my third year in college, it helps a lot, learning from different experiences and different schools, that's a factor. And, obviously, the system and the offense we run here, and Ali believing in me and working with me, personally, one-on-one as a player has helped a lot too. I always knew ... I could play and I had game, but coming here, I feel like they just really helped me harness that." What better place to find people who believe in you than back at home. "Sometimes you need somebody to believe in you, and I think Carey was waiting for that," Farokhmanesh said. "I think he knows he's got a staff here that believes in him, that trusts in him, that's willing to grow with him too."
